name: TI Kuala Lumpur assembly and test factory expansion

parties.name: Malaysian Investment Development Authority
parties.note: Federal investment agency that announced and backed the expansion; no incentive amount is published.

summary: Texas Instruments plans a new assembly and test factory in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, by converting a building it bought next to its existing Kuala Lumpur plant, with potential investment of up to MYR 9.6 billion and more than 1 million sq ft of cleanroom. Announced in June 2023, construction was expected to begin later that year and production as early as 2025. No cited source reports construction or production.

metrics.note: Potential investment to convert the building into an assembly and test factory.
Site of the building TI bought next to its existing Kuala Lumpur factory.
Additional local jobs at full build.

milestones.note: Construction expected to start later in 2023.

sources.title: Texas Instruments to expand manufacturing operations in Malaysia

notes: Searches in November 2026 found no report of construction progress or a production start for this factory, so the record stays announced; the 2025 production target is a planned milestone that no source has confirmed. The operator has not published a name for the factory.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Added the 18-acre site area stated in TI's announcement; no corrections were needed and no newer reporting on construction or production was found.
